title: Symmetry-breaking line defects embedded to a 3D $O(N)$ critical bulk
authors: Shuai Yang, Liang-dong Hu, Yan Chen, W. Zhu
abstract: While spontaneous breaking of a discrete symmetry in one-dimensional classical systems with short-range interactions is absent, it is expected that a line defect embedded in a bulk criticality exhibits a stable discrete symmetry spontaneous breaking. Here, we investigate the behavior of a pinning-field line defect immersed in a 3D bulk that remains tuned to the $O(N)$ Wilson-Fisher critical point. Employing the fuzzy sphere technique, we provide convincing evidence of the existence of stable defect conformal fixed points, and we demonstrate their renormalization group stability by showing no relevant operator and less effective degrees of freedom than that at bulk fixed point via $g$-function. Moreover, we investigate the defect domain wall operator for various $N$, and we identify that it becomes irrelevance for $N\gtrsim 3$ but it is relevant for $N<3$.These evidence indicate that a one-dimensional defect coupled to a critical bulk cannot support a stable symmetry spontaneously broken defect fixed point due to domain wall proliferation for $N<3$ Wilson-Fisher universality, while in the case of $N \gtrsim 3$ a symmetry broken defect is possible.
summary: This work theoretically examines the stability of symmetry-breaking line defects embedded in a 3D O(N) critical bulk. Using advanced CFT and RG methods, the authors determine that stable symmetry breaking is only possible when the symmetry dimension N is greater than or equal to 3. This provides a quantitative criterion for defect stability in critical quantum matter.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a line defect embedded in a 3D O(N) critical bulk can support a stable spontaneously symmetry-breaking (SSB) defect fixed point, contrasting with known instabilities in 1D systems.
main_result: A stable SSB defect fixed point is possible only for $N \gtrsim 3$, while for $N < 3$, domain wall proliferation prevents such stability.
method: The study employs Defect Conformal Field Theory (dCFT) techniques, utilizing the fuzzy sphere method and Renormalization Group (RG) analysis via the g-function to test stability.
model_or_system: The system models a line defect immersed in a 3D bulk tuned to the O(N) Wilson-Fisher critical point. The stability is analyzed by considering the effect of domain-wall operators and pinning fields.
key_observables: Scaling dimensions ($\Delta$) of primary operators, the defect $g$-function, and the relevance/irrelevance of the domain-wall operator.
important_parameters: The dimensionality $N$ of the symmetry group, and the critical exponents associated with the O(N) Wilson-Fisher universality class.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the fuzzy-sphere regularization technique for general N, and the stability criteria are based on the RG flow analysis of the defect operators.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically compares RG flow diagrams showing stable vs. unstable SSB fixed points based on the value of N relative to a critical value.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by contrasting 1D vs. 3D defect stability, then applies the fuzzy sphere technique and RG analysis to the O(N) Wilson-Fisher model, deriving conditions for stable defect fixed points based on N.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of CFT and RG techniques to defect lines in critical systems provides powerful tools for understanding boundary physics, which is relevant to engineered quantum materials or interfaces in AMO physics.
